key_insight: AEAPTMS amino-silane passivation makes mixed-halide perovskite surfaces electronically more uniform, reducing grain-boundary barriers and improving photovoltage dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This suggests molecular passivation can directly improve perovskite solar cell stability and voltage output by smoothing surface potential landscapes at the nanoscale.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy measured dark CPD and light-induced SPV on perovskite thin films.
Compared passivated vs unpassivated films to quantify surface-potential homogeneity and photovoltage stabilization.
Used wavelength-dependent SPV and grain-boundary/grain-interior separation to probe sub-bandgap disorder and local barriers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports CPD distribution narrowing from ~45.7 to ~14.6 mV, SPV increasing from ~345 to ~417 mV, and stabilization time decreasing from ~840 to ~470 s after AEAPTMS treatment.
watch_item: These results are based on thin-film nanoscale measurements, so translating the observed surface improvements into full device performance requires careful validation under operating conditions.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
